answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Lockstep. Each identity’s action history is hashed into a kernel at epoch close; the next epoch must reproduce a bounded behavioural distance from it. Clusters whose many identities pivot in lockstep reveal a vine of shared control, and suspicious nodes are throttled. Thresholds shift by an umber margin derived from prior variance. Attackers must sustain independent, plausible histories per identity across epochs, multiplying operational cost per account.
